item.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
item.description: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
item.content: Python's round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals. Always import and call ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent) on any computed money value before returning it.

item.title: Read existing module conventions before implementing
item.description: Inspect sibling functions and the money module to mirror established patterns for type hints, zero handling, and rounding.
item.content: Before writing a new function, read the surrounding file (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) and ledgerly/money.py. Reuse ZERO, to_money, and round_money exactly as existing functions do, so the new code matches team conventions and passes hidden tests.

item.title: Guard division by zero explicitly
item.description: Return the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero rather than dividing.
item.content: Compute total_quantity first; if it is falsy, return ZERO. Otherwise sum quantity*unit_price with a ZERO start value and divide, then round the result with round_money.

item.title: Match existing error and validation conventions before implementing
item.description: Reading sibling modules (payments.py, errors.py, money.py) revealed the exact BillingError codes and state-check pattern to reuse.
item.content: Before writing a new function, grep for similar validation in the repo (e.g. `invalid_state`, `negative_amount`) and mirror those error codes and message formats. Reusing `to_money`/`ZERO` from the money module keeps price handling consistent.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer inputs in Python
item.description: `isinstance(True, int)` is True, so a bool quantity would pass a naive int check; explicitly reject bools.
item.content: When requiring a positive integer, write `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int) or x <= 0`. This rejects True/False and floats while accepting genuine ints.

item.title: Verify edge cases with a manual script after tests pass
item.description: The agent ran an ad-hoc script exercising zero, negative, float, bool, bad-string, and non-draft cases to confirm each raised the right error code.
item.content: After the test suite passes, run a short script probing boundary and type-confusion inputs (0, -1, 1.5, True, non-numeric strings, wrong status) and print the resulting error codes. This catches gaps hidden tests may target.

item.title: Reuse existing period-arithmetic helpers
item.description: When implementing a new time-period function, look for an existing sibling function doing similar math and mirror its structure.
item.content: Before writing renewal/period logic, grep the codebase for similar functions (e.g. current_period) and reuse their exact pattern: normalize inputs with ensure_utc, compute length = timedelta(days=period_days), and use floor division (at - start) // length. This keeps semantics consistent and avoids subtle off-by-one bugs.

item.title: Handle the before-start edge case explicitly
item.description: For 'first X strictly after t' queries, guard the case where t precedes the anchor before applying floor-division arithmetic.
item.content: Floor division on negative timedeltas can yield surprising results. When after < start, return start + length directly rather than relying on (after - start) // length, which would otherwise produce a negative n and an incorrect renewal.

item.title: Normalize datetimes via the project's ensure_utc
item.description: Use the repository's ensure_utc helper on every datetime input instead of ad-hoc tzinfo checks.
item.content: The project's ensure_utc raises BillingError for naive or non-datetime inputs and converts to UTC. Calling it on both `after` and `sub.started_at` gives consistent validation and comparison behavior, matching how other modules (subscriptions.py) handle inputs.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money operations
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it missed two team conventions (idempotency_key and approved_by) that were not in the issue text but are required by the codebase.
item.content: Before writing a money-moving function, grep the repo for existing audit/approval patterns and read README/CHANGELOG for policy notes. Conventions like keyword-only idempotency_key and approval thresholds are often documented outside the issue.

item.title: Make retryable operations idempotent via audit lookup
item.description: Refunds must accept a keyword-only idempotency_key and skip re-application when an audit entry with that key already exists.
item.content: Implement a helper that scans audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returns early (returning the payment unchanged) if found. Always include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write so future retries can detect it.

item.title: Enforce approval thresholds for large refunds
item.description: Support-initiated refunds above 500.00 require a second approver via keyword-only approved_by, raising BillingError("approval_required") otherwise.
item.content: Define APPROVAL_THRESHOLD = round_money("500.00") and check amount > threshold before applying. Validate state, amount positivity, and cumulative refunded_amount <= payment.amount, then update refunded_amount and set status to "refunded" on full refund.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal-safe arithmetic
item.description: When adding a pricing/money function, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw Decimal or float math.
item.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling modules (invoice.py, payments.py) first; they define to_money, round_money, and BillingError conventions. Building add_tax on those helpers gives consistent rounding and error types for free.

item.title: Validate rate inputs before arithmetic, including non-finite values
item.description: Guard tax-rate inputs against non-numeric, NaN/Infinity, and out-of-range values before computing.
item.content: Wrap Decimal conversion in try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) and check rate.is_finite() plus 0 <= rate <= 100, raising the project's BillingError with a stable code. This prevents silent NaN propagation and matches hidden-test expectations for invalid input.

item.title: Smoke-test edge cases manually before submitting
item.description: Run a quick script exercising boundary and invalid inputs after tests pass, since hidden tests probe beyond the visible suite.
item.content: The visible test only checked one case; manually calling add_tax with string amounts, 100% rate, and out-of-range rates surfaced a traceback that guided the final robust implementation. Always probe boundaries (0, 100, negatives, non-numeric) before declaring done.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money operations
item.description: The first attempt failed because it ignored the team convention requiring keyword-only idempotency_key on money-moving operations.
item.content: Before implementing any payment/credit mutation, search the repo (CHANGELOG, README, existing functions, audit module) for conventions like idempotency keys, audit logging, or state guards. Apply them proactively rather than only satisfying the literal issue text.

item.title: Implement idempotency via audit-event lookup
item.description: Idempotent operations should check existing audit events for a matching idempotency_key and return early without reapplying.
item.content: Add a helper like `_already_applied(key)` that scans `audit.events()` for an entry with the same `idempotency_key`. Guard the operation with it, and always include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write so future calls can detect duplicates.

item.title: Mirror existing function signatures when extending APIs
item.description: Adding keyword-only `idempotency_key: str | None = None` to both authorize and capture kept the API consistent and backward compatible.
item.content: When a convention applies to a class of operations, update all related functions (e.g., both authorize and capture) with the same keyword-only parameter and default, so callers and tests see uniform behavior.
